name: Ultimate Brawler Championship
epitaph: The first of the four belts on the fed's own Champions page, which lists them from the most important to the least. The page, captured 14 February 2003, reads "[none]" for its current and its previous holder, and no match on the fed's three Jurisdiction shows (7, 14 and 21 December 2002) puts it on the line: no holder is recorded.
notes: Source: the fed's own Champions page (ubc.wrestleonline.org/champions.php, Wayback capture of 14 February 2003). The trophy Brett Wayne lifts at the close of the last Jurisdiction card (21 December 2002) is the fed's "Future Brawler Trophy Award" ("FBA Trophy"), which its own news of that day says the match was for; it is not this belt. The fed's own news of 1 January 2003 books this belt for that Saturday's Jurisdiction card (a three-way elimination match, Chris "AK" Carter, Tommy Grady and Brett Wayne); no surviving record shows that card was held.

name: Dual Combat Championship
epitaph: The last of the four belts on the fed's own Champions page, and the only one it gives plural holders ("Current Holders: [none]"): a tag-team belt. The page, captured 14 February 2003, reads "[none]" for its current and its previous holders, and no match on the fed's three Jurisdiction shows (7, 14 and 21 December 2002) puts it on the line: no holder is recorded.
notes: Source: the fed's own Champions page (ubc.wrestleonline.org/champions.php, Wayback capture of 14 February 2003). The fed's own news of 1 January 2003 books this belt for that Saturday's Jurisdiction card (a three-way tag-team match, Krisis and Violent B, the Kingz of Africa and the Heart Throbs); no surviving record shows that card was held. The relaunch posts of 23 January 2003 (captured on the fed's front page, 14 February 2003) announce a 64-man Dual Combat tournament for it, of which only the qualifying brackets survive.
